item.title: U.S. and Canada enforcement blitzes sideline 124 drivers and 226 vehicles
item.description:
Federal, state and local authorities placed at least 124 drivers and 226 commercial vehicles out of service during enforcement actions from mid‑September through Oct. 1 across the United States and Canada. One of the largest actions, Operation Saturday Night Fever, generated 552 inspections that sidelined 78 drivers and 25 vehicles.
In Illinois, state police conducted a two‑day hazardous‑materials detail that generated 532 inspections and led to dozens of drivers and vehicles being placed out of service. Arizona troopers carried out 46 inspections along Interstate 10, resulting in more than a dozen drivers and vehicles being sidelined. Elsewhere, inspectors flagged unsafe brakes and tires, invalid licenses, and drivers observed watching videos while behind the wheel. The blitz also covered hazardous‑materials checks, credential reviews, electronic logging device inspections, fatigue and distracted‑driving assessments, and cargo securement reviews. Federal, state and local agencies coordinated the effort, with the FMCSA, DHS and numerous state police departments participating in the overnight Operation Saturday Night Fever. Authorities said the goal was to identify and remove unsafe trucks and drivers from the nation’s highways before they could cause accidents. Carriers receiving out‑of‑service orders must repair defects and pass re‑inspection before returning to work. The effort reflected a broader push by regulators to tighten oversight of commercial vehicle operations during the fall shipping season.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/us-canada-truck-enforcement-blitzes-sideline-350-drivers-vehicles)

item.title: Shopify adds discount scheduling and testing to Rollouts on October 2, 2026
item.description:
Shopify introduced the ability to include discounts in Rollouts on October 2, 2026, letting merchants schedule, test, and launch discount changes alongside theme and checkout updates. The feature enables merchants to run coordinated campaigns, compare offer performance, and expand successful tests to broader traffic.
Merchants can launch a new offer to a portion of online store traffic via Rollouts. They can increase the audience share for that offer when they decide to expand. The expansion occurs when the merchant is ready to roll out the offer more broadly. Merchants can test discount changes against their existing offers. They can review conversion results in the Rollouts dashboard. The review helps decide which offer to keep. Discount changes can be scheduled to go live at the same time as theme updates. Discount changes can be scheduled to go live at the same time as checkout updates. All three updates launch together in a single rollout. Each discount’s existing customer eligibility rules continue to apply when used in Rollouts. Merchants can continue to use discount start dates for standalone promotions outside of Rollouts. Merchants can continue to use discount end dates for standalone promotions outside of Rollouts. Merchants can continue to use both discount start and end dates for standalone promotions outside of Rollouts. For further guidance, Shopify directs users to its help documentation on discounts scheduling and testing.
Source: Shopify Changelog (https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/schedule-and-test-discounts-with-rollouts)

item.title: Nike extends turnaround timeline amid layoffs and sales declines
item.description:
Nike said on Thursday it will lay off an unspecified number of workers next year after reporting a 4% drop in quarterly revenue to $11.2 billion. Converse sales fell 28% and Greater China revenue dropped 22%, while Nike warned that full‑year revenue could slip by a high‑single‑digit percentage.
Under the Pace plan, Nike will combine its geographic units into three groups: the Americas (North America and Latin America), APGC (Asia Pacific and Greater China), and EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa). The company said it will invest in a more flexible supply chain, open a Nike campus in Bengaluru, India, and shift resources toward product innovation, brand storytelling and consumer connection. Nike’s CEO Elliott Hill said the restructuring is meant to accelerate the Sport Offense strategy but will lead to job cuts and a longer turnaround than analysts expected.
“China and Converse are the two most obvious — indeed, between them they account for almost 86% of the group’s net sales decline,” Neil Saunders said.
Pace is Nike’s third restructuring program since fiscal 2024, following earlier efforts that have yet to deliver operating leverage. Analysts noted that the Win Now strategy, initially slated for completion by the end of 2025, was later pushed to the end of 2026 and now lacks a clear new timeline.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/nike-turnaround-visibility-very-low-layoffs-sales-declines-q1-earnings/832015)

item.title: Payoneer renews Etsy partnership through 2029 to serve sellers in 16 markets
item.description:
Payoneer said it has renewed its partnership with Etsy through 2029, extending the collaboration that began in 2023. Under the three-year agreement, Payoneer will remain a strategic payments partner for Etsy sellers across 16 markets in Asia, Europe, South America and the Middle East, enabling tens of thousands of sellers to receive cross-border payouts. The financial terms of the renewed partnership were not disclosed by either company.
Payoneer noted that sellers in volatile markets rely on the partnership to access global customers and manage cross-border earnings. Maksym Gopanchuk, founder of Ukraine‑based KGUmusic and MG Leather Work, said roughly 80 percent of his sales come from the United States, with additional sales in Europe, the UK, Asia and Australia. Ya Wen, senior vice president of global marketplaces at Payoneer, said small businesses are increasingly selling across borders, currencies and markets, making financial infrastructure vital for their success.
“When local market conditions can change literally overnight, access to the global market and reliable international partners make it possible to keep moving forward. Etsy helps our brands reach customers across different countries, while Payoneer provides the payment infrastructure that makes our international sales possible,” Maksym Gopanchuk, founder of Ukraine‑based KGUmusic and MG Leather Work said.
“A reliable payments experience is essential to helping Etsy sellers across the globe grow and thrive,” Megan Oxman, senior director of product at Etsy said.
Payoneer and Etsy first partnered in 2023 to enable cross-border payouts for sellers. The original collaboration aimed to help sellers receive earnings across borders and grow globally.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/etsy-payoneer-renew-partnership-1239301491)

item.title: Weavabel launches closed-loop recycling system for poly bags
item.description:
Weavabel, a UK-based trims and packaging specialist, has recently introduced a closed-loop recycling system that collects used poly bags from fashion brands and reprocesses them into new packaging. The system is designed to help brands comply with upcoming EU packaging rules without requiring them to build their own recycling infrastructure.
Fashion brands order the poly bags from Weavabel’s nearest warehouse, use them to pack garments, and ship the packed inventory to distribution centres. After garments reach stores, the brands gather the used bags from their stores and return them to the distribution centres, where the bags are sorted and baled. Weavabel then picks up the baled waste by truck, consolidates it across the EU and United Kingdom, and sends it to a licensed importer for sorting, shredding and initial processing. The processed material undergoes polymer blending, is pelletised, and blown into film at Weavabel’s production plant, where it is formed into new poly bags for reuse.
“Poly bags have always been treated as disposable, but that thinking doesn’t hold up anymore,” Saqib Ihsan, head of regulatory compliance and sustainability at Weavabel said.
“Regulation is moving fast, and most brands are being asked to prove circularity, not just claim it—so we built this loop to give them a real, traceable answer. It works with the way poly bags already move through warehouses, factories and distribution centres, so nothing has to change on the brand’s side except where the waste ends up,” Saqib Ihsan, head of regulatory compliance and sustainability at Weavabel said.
The European Union’s Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation and Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation are pushing fashion and lifestyle brands to demonstrate material circularity, while existing collection systems remain fragmented and recycling infrastructure limited.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/weavabel-closed-loop-sytem-poly-bag-eu-circularity-1239303024)

item.title: AutoZone shifts focus to U.S. and Mexico distribution network for fiscal 2027
item.description:
AutoZone said it will concentrate its growth on the U.S. and Mexico while slowing Brazil expansion, aiming to complete its domestic distribution upgrades by fiscal year 2027, according to CEO Philip Daniele’s Sept. 22 earnings call. The retailer plans to spend about $1.5 billion in capital expenditures this year, mainly on store growth and its hub and mega hub network.
AutoZone reported that its U.S. distribution center expansion is finished, comprising two new distribution facilities and two direct import facilities. The company operates 172 mega hub stores and intends to open more than 40 additional mega hubs in fiscal year 2027, building toward a goal of 300 mega hubs over the next three years. Jamere Jackson, CFO of Customer Satisfaction, noted that roughly 2,000 commercial programs linked to the mega hub network generate 16% higher annual sales than other programs. In Mexico, AutoZone has opened an expanded distribution center in Monterrey that is now double its previous size and has broken ground on another planned facility there.
“There are approximately 2,000 commercial programs that are linked to a mega hub network. These programs sell 16% more annually than the balance of the commercial programs in the chain,” Jamere Jackson, CFO of Customer Satisfaction said.
“We opened our new expanded Monterrey, Mexico, distribution center and broke ground on another planned DC in Mexico,” Philip Daniele, President and CEO said.
AutoZone’s supply chain investments began in 2020 and are now in the final stages of completion. Previously, the retailer had aimed to operate 200 hubs in 2024 before raising its target to 300 mega hubs.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/autozone-hones-in-on-domestic-distribution-network/831931)

item.title: Latitude Global settles payments in under two minutes via stablecoins
item.description:
Latitude Global offers payment settlement in less than two minutes, according to CEO Cyril Mathew in a Sept. 21 interview. The company’s network reaches about 50 countries and it aims to enter about 200 in the coming years. Latitude has raised $43 million in equity funding, including $35 million announced last month.
Latitude provides fiat on‑and‑off ramps that let neobanks and other firms use stablecoins to transfer money within their apps, and it is focused on meeting clear demand for more emerging markets in Southeast Asia and Africa. The firm employs 14 people and holds money‑transmitter licenses in 45 U.S. states, with applications pending for the remaining five. Founded in January 2025 by former Stripe crypto executive Cyril Mathew, ex‑Stripe engineer Brian Wrightson (CTO), and former Zero Hash leader Vivek Morzaria. Latitude supports USDC and USDT stablecoins for its cross‑border transfers, and Mathew is based in Spring, Texas, a Houston suburb.
“We support several: USDC (Circle), we support USDT (Tether),” Cyril Mathew, CEO said.
“There doesn’t need to be 1,000 stablecoins or 1,000 blockchains, and I’m using a high number on purpose,” Cyril Mathew, CEO said.
Mathew, a former Stripe cryptocurrency executive, established Latitude in January 2025 with Brian Wrightson, a former Stripe engineer who serves as chief technology officer, and Vivek Morzaria, a former executive with Zero Hash, a cryptocurrency infrastructure startup. Latitude has raised $43 million in equity funding, including $35 million announced last month.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/how-stablecoins-speed-intl-payments-crypto-cross-border-emerging-markets/831935)

item.title: Retailers see UK deposit return scheme as chance to boost footfall
item.description:
Exchange for Change has set out intended producer fees for the UK’s Deposit Return Scheme, stating that producers will pay no fee for the first 15 months from October 2027 to December 2028. From January 2029 the fee is projected at 0.6p per aluminium or steel container and 2.3p per PET container, with the rates set to be reviewed and reconfirmed in May 2027.
Powers says retailers can treat the scheme as a compliance cost or use reverse vending machines to draw customers who return containers for a voucher. He notes that children returning bottles for pocket money may spend the voucher on high‑margin items such as magazines or confectionery. At forecourts, a large reverse vending machine could generate a £100 voucher for a customer bringing many empties, which could then be spent on fuel or store goods. He also warns that long queues or unemptied machines will drive shoppers away, making machine reliability a competitive factor. Using a hypothetical one million containers each with a 20p deposit, Powers calculates that a retailer could see £800,000 of working capital moving through the business before the handling fee is applied. He advises retailers to first check their exemption status, decide whether to operate a return point, choose between manual systems or RVMs, look for grants, and consider the impact on cash flow.
“You can use this to attract footfall,” Bill Powers, chairman of DRS International said.
“If I turn up at a store and there’s a queue for the machine, consumers hate that,” Bill Powers, chairman of DRS International said.
The scheme is set to launch in October 2027.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/drs-retailers)

item.title: Daimler Truck outlines Europe’s need for 35,000 megawatt chargers by 2030
item.description:
Daimler Truck said Europe needs 35,000 megawatt charging points by 2030 to shift battery‑electric and hydrogen trucks from early adopters to mainstream fleets, speaking at its Media Night in Hanover ahead of IAA Transportation 2026. Mercedes‑Benz Trucks held about 38% of Europe’s market for locally CO₂‑free medium‑ and heavy‑duty trucks in the first half of 2026, and its eActros 600 models have logged over 160 million kilometres since series production began at the end of 2024.
Europe currently has fewer than 2,000 public truck charge points, most of them standard CCS units. To meet CO₂ targets, Daimler Truck says Europe will need 35,000 megawatt‑charging points and about 1,000 hydrogen stations suitable for trucks by 2030. In Germany, the CO₂‑based road toll gives electric trucks an advantage of roughly 33 to 35 cents per kilometre over diesel, while only 13 of the EU’s 27 member states have adopted such tolls.
“Today, there are over 60 electric or zero-emission trucks available in the market, and over 25 different zero-emission bus models from us and from our competitors,” Karin Rådström, CEO, Daimler Truck said.
“We are proud to have more than 200 battery-electric trucks on the road, but the truth is we run more than 15,000,” Stefan Hohm, Chief Development Officer, Dachser said.
In 2025, heavy‑duty battery‑electric trucks accounted for 2% of Europe’s market, and the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association reported that electrically chargeable trucks above 3.5 tonnes reached 4.2% of the EU market, up from 2.3% the previous year. Daimler Truck estimates that about 35% of new trucks must run on batteries or hydrogen by 2030 to meet EU CO₂ targets.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/daimler-truck-scale-electric-trucks-europe)

item.title: FTC, Utah, Nevada Sue Lens.com Over Hidden Fees That Double Lens Prices
item.description:
Today, the Federal Trade Commission, joined by the attorneys general of Utah and Nevada, sued contact‑lens retailer Lens.com for allegedly charging hidden “Taxes & fees” that double the advertised price and have cost consumers hundreds of millions of dollars. The complaint alleges the fees are concealed below the visible checkout screen, prompting consumers to click “Continue” without seeing the extra charge.
The “Taxes & fees” label suggests a government tax, but many states exempt contact lenses from sales tax or have none, so the charge is not a tax. Lens.com applies the same hidden fee to its AutoRefill subscription plan, which automatically bills consumers for recurring shipments without clearly disclosing the charge before collecting payment information. The complaint cites violations of the FTC Act, ROSCA, GLB Act, Utah CSPA, Utah ARCA, and Nevada DTPA, notes the Commission voted 2-0 to authorize the filing, and says the case was filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Nevada.
“Lens.com advertised one price for contact lenses but charged a substantially higher price at checkout, deceiving consumers about the cost of this healthcare necessity,” Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection said.
Lens.com has been running a long-running deceptive pricing scheme, according to the complaint. The complaint also notes that the company has used similar tactics in its AutoRefill subscription plan.
Source: FTC Press Releases (https://ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/10/ftc-states-sue-lenscom-misrepresenting-price-contact-lenses-search-ads-its-website)

item.title: FedEx launches $20 Authenticated Delivery service for high-value shipments
item.description:
FedEx introduced its Authenticated Delivery service on September 16, charging $20 per package for select expedited services in the U.S. and Canada. The option uses QR code authentication to release packages only to authorized recipients, aiming to curb fraud and theft for luxury goods, electronics, healthcare, aerospace and collectibles.
Upon delivery, the recipient must show the QR code to the FedEx driver, who scans and validates it before releasing the package. The service is available with FedEx First Overnight, Priority Overnight, Standard Overnight, 2Day, 2Day A.M. and Express Saver for domestic shipments, and with most international package services except FedEx International Ground. Authenticated Delivery shipments cannot be subject to address changes, hold‑at‑location requests or redirect‑to‑hold, but recipients may place a temporary vacation hold on the package. If a delivery attempt fails, FedEx may reattempt up to three times; after the third unsuccessful attempt the package is returned to the sender. The QR code is generated at shipment creation and sent to the recipient via email or SMS, ensuring only the intended party can authorize release.
“The future of delivery isn’t just moving packages quickly. It’s about building greater trust throughout the delivery process,” Neil Gibson, FedEx SVP of global customer experience said.
The launch of FedEx Authenticated Delivery marks another way the carrier is pushing to draw higher-value packages into its network to boost profitability. Rival UPS has also bolstered its options for more secure package delivery in recent years; its DeliveryDefense tool weighs loss frequency and delivery attempts to predict successful delivery likelihood and lets shippers reroute at‑risk shipments to alternate drop‑off locations.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/fedex-rolls-out-added-security-option-for-select-deliveries/831596)

item.title: Georgia Ports Authority’s Savannah terminal hits 60% completion
item.description:
Georgia Ports Authority announced that its $1.6 billion redevelopment of Savannah’s Ocean Terminal surpassed the 60% completion mark, with a 2,650-foot berth now finished. The project will expand the terminal’s annual capacity from 200,000 to 1.75 million twenty-foot equivalent units.
Work continues on the container-yard, with the first phase slated for completion in mid-fall 2027 and the full yard expected by the end of 2028. The truck gate is already operational and will ultimately feature 12 inbound lanes and six outbound lanes. A $29 million overpass now directs departing trucks straight to U.S. 17 and Interstate 16, keeping them off nearby neighborhood streets. The renovated berth is ready to handle the largest container vessels calling at Savannah. The project also includes upgrades to rail connections that will improve intermodal transfers between the port and inland distribution centers. Environmental mitigations were built into the plan, including stormwater management systems and habitat restoration near the terminal.
“The renovated berth is fully completed and ready for big ships,” Griff Lynch, Chief Executive, Georgia Ports Authority said.
The Ocean Terminal redevelopment is part of Georgia Ports Authority’s 10-year port master plan, which calls for roughly $5 billion in capacity investments across the state. Under that plan, the authority intends to add five container berths in Savannah and one roll-on/roll-off berth in Brunswick. In August, Savannah moved 529,523 TEUs, with loaded exports up 4.2% and imports up 1.5% year-over-year.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/savannah-port-project-passes-60-complete-mark)

item.title: Morrisons launches UK supermarket-first Click & Collect lockers at Skipton store
item.description:
Morrisons has launched a new multi-temperature Click & Collect locker system at its Skipton store in North Yorkshire, extending Click & Collect operating hours by two hours a day as part of the trial. The trial extends Click & Collect operating hours by two hours each day, giving customers more collection windows.
Customers receive a unique six-digit code to enter at the locker terminal, and their shopping is pre-loaded into ambient, chilled and frozen compartments ahead of arrival. Chilled goods are kept between 3°C and 5°C, frozen products between -18°C and -20°C, and ambient groceries at 16°C, while larger compartments can hold up to three bags. For age‑restricted items the locker stays locked until a colleague verifies the customer’s ID under Challenge 25 rules, and a help button linked to VoCoVo lets shoppers speak directly with store colleagues. The system can allocate multiple locker doors to a single customer for larger orders, enabling flexible collection of big shops.
“We know customers want Click & Collect to be quick, convenient and flexible, and our new locker solution is designed to be exactly that. By bringing StrongPoint’s proven technology to our stores, we can offer more collection slots while removing the wait for colleagues to bring orders to customers’ cars,” Charlotte Exell, Morrisons group online director said.
The grocer said the new model would also replace its current process of handing over loose shopping, with Click & Collect orders instead pre-packed into paper bags. Morrisons has also integrated VoCoVo communication technology into the lockers, allowing shoppers to connect directly with store colleagues through a help button if they need assistance.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/morrisons-launches-uk-supermarket-first-grocery-collection-lockers)

item.title: Nike plans job cuts after China sales plunge 26%
item.description:
Nike announced a new round of job cuts and a global restructuring starting in 2027 after its Greater China sales fell 26% in the latest quarter. The company said the restructuring will generate around £1.9bn in savings by fiscal 2031 and sent its shares down 8.5% in extended trading.
Nike will reduce unspecified roles from 2027 and shift from four operating regions to three: the Americas, Asia Pacific and Greater China, and Europe, Middle East and Africa. It also plans to open a new campus in India, cut Jordan retro launches, and withdraw online sales rights from some major wholesale partners in China starting January. In the quarter, North American sales rose 2% on a constant‑currency basis and gross margin increased 60 basis points to 42.8%.
“its performance-focused business was not yet large enough to offset weaker trading across its sportswear, Jordan and Greater China divisions,” Elliott Hill, chief executive said.
“the company would begin providing updated targets through the financial year from November as the restructuring progresses,” Elliott Hill, chief executive said.
Nike has been facing declining sales in Greater China for nine straight quarters and has been under pressure from both international sportswear rivals and domestic Chinese brands. Under CEO Elliott Hill, the company has tried to revive growth by focusing on running and repairing relationships with wholesale partners after previously prioritising its direct‑to‑consumer business.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/nike-plots-further-job-cuts-as-china-sales-plunge-26)

item.title: Angara readies just-in-time model for Cyber 5 flexibility
item.description:
In October 2026, online-only jewelry retailer Angara is preparing for the five-day Cyber 5 period by boosting flexibility in its just-in-time model. The retailer notes that consumer preferences can shift within five to six months, leaving traditional inventory plans outdated. Angara holds the 363rd spot in the Top 1000 Database and ranks 192nd in Digital Commerce 360’s AI Rankings.
Angara’s just‑in‑time production enables it to monitor real‑time signals — such as which gemstone, cut, metal or price point shoppers are clicking on — and immediately shift manufacturing focus to those items without building up finished stock. During the Cyber 5 window the company prioritizes expanding factory shifts, upgrading order‑management software redundancy and ensuring its website can handle traffic spikes, treating these elements as core inventory. It also broadens its catalog of customizable options, letting buyers choose metal type, gemstone quality, carat weight and whether the stone is natural or lab‑grown, all presented through an intuitive configurator. To support decision‑making, Angara adds educational content — such as guides on the 4Cs, carat visualizers and metal‑care tips — directly on product pages, aiming to reduce bounce rates and lift average order value.
“Because we manufacture just in time, we’re not sitting on large amounts of finished inventory. We can see what customers are responding to — whether that’s a particular gemstone, shape, metal or price point — and adjust very quickly,” Ankur Daga, co‑founder and CEO of Angara said.
In 2025, Angara learned that companies able to listen and adapt in real time gain a distinct advantage over those trying to predict customer behavior months ahead. The retailer also found that traditional jewelry makers typically make holiday inventory decisions five or six months in advance, which can leave them unable to react to fast‑changing tastes.
Source: Digital Commerce 360 (https://digitalcommerce360.com/2026/10/01/angara-cyber-5-consumer-behavior)

item.title: DoorDash launches agentic ordering waitlist for offices, cites five partners
item.description:
DoorDash opened a waitlist for its agentic ordering MCP for corporate offices as of Sept. 30, naming SpaceX, Cognition, Vercel, Mercor and Tempo as early partners. The Model Context Protocol lets companies connect internal AI agents to DoorDash for automated office orders such as lunch catering and supply restocks.
DoorDash launched the command line interface for agentic ordering in beta in July, allowing individual developers to link DoorDash ordering to their personal agents for recurring grocery orders and preference‑based suggestions. Accepted waitlist participants receive access at the company level, after which each employee must sign into an individual DoorDash account to accept the terms of service and connect their AI agents. The beta remains limited in scope, permitting companies to place orders only for their teams rather than for broader consumer markets.
“enables individual developers to connect DoorDash ordering capabilities to their personal agents,” Andy Fang, co-founder and director at DoorDash said.
“In fact, one of the biggest use cases we saw was automating their office work,” Andy Fang, co-founder and director at DoorDash said.
Prior to this announcement, DoorDash showcased new drone delivery and its Dasher Returns service at the Dash Forward event in San Francisco. The company had also introduced a beta command line interface for agentic ordering in July to enable developers to connect DoorDash to personal agents.
Source: Digital Commerce 360 (https://digitalcommerce360.com/2026/10/01/doordash-expands-access-to-agentic-ordering-for-offices-corporate-customers)

item.title: GLP-1 Users Report Jeans as First Casualty, Sparking Wardrobe Overhaul
item.description:
A Trimi Health survey of 737 U.S. adults using GLP-1 medications found that 90 percent see denim as disrupted and 42 percent say their jeans are now completely unwearable. The average cost to rebuild a wardrobe with fitting clothes is $328, and more than half of respondents now shop retailers they never used before treatment. Seventy percent of GLP-1 users have left the plus‑size stores they previously patronized, with Lane Bryant down 72 percent and Torrid down 65 percent in share.
Free People doubled its share among surveyed shoppers from 5 percent to 10 percent, while 27 percent said they traded up to a contemporary, premium or athleisure brand they had not bought before. Sixty‑eight percent donate unwanted clothing, 54 percent store items ‘just in case,’ 28 percent resell them, and 46 percent have thrown away clothes that no longer fit.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sj-denim/trimi-glp-1-survey-jeans-weight-loss-plus-size-retailers-1239302866)

item.title: China’s liner‑shipping connectivity index reaches 1,347.6 in September 2026
item.description:
China’s liner‑shipping connectivity index rose to 1,347.6 in September 2026, more than doubling the scores of the economies with the next highest connectivity. The advantage has remained durable since 2023 and the United States and Malaysia were among the highest‑ranked economies.
The index aggregates vessel calls, port capacity, carrier and service availability, the size of the largest ships and the number of countries reached by direct services. At the regional level, the leading economies in each major market area showed mixed performance, with some gaining and others losing ground. Smaller and less‑connected economies experienced the sharpest percentage swings, with some posting large gains and others steep declines.
China’s connectivity advantage has remained durable since 2023 and increased further through September 2026. While major hub economies recorded limited year‑over‑year changes, smaller and less‑connected economies showed the sharpest percentage swings.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/new-un-data-china-widens-lead-in-liner-shipping-connectivity)

item.title: Intermodal hits highs with 8% growth as truckload rejections hold near 14%
item.description:
Domestic intermodal container volumes reached all-time highs with 8% year over year growth while truckload tender rejection rates held near 14% The shift signals freight moving from truck to rail, countering a typical early-October volume dip
Refrigerated freight gains support from active harvest season demand that typically persists through January. Rising diesel costs are pushing dry van, flatbed, and refrigerated spot rates higher, while rejection rates remain fuel‑agnostic. Smaller fleets with heavy spot market exposure absorb the costs when full fuel pass through is blocked, squeezing margins. Strickland warned that the rail network’s fixed infrastructure may struggle to sustain the 8% intermodal growth long term
“I know a lot of this freight is going intermodal at this point too,” Zach Strickland, analyst said.
“It does not look sustainable to me at this point,” Zach Strickland, analyst said.
Truckload markets normally see an early-October lull, but this year tender rejection rates have held near 14%. Intermodal volumes have posted consistent multi-year gains before reaching a new all-time high with 8% year over year growth
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/intermodal-hits-all-time-highs-as-truckload-stays-tight)

item.title: Kodiak picks IKEA for driverless freight launch in Texas, Louisiana by 2025
item.description:
Kodiak has named IKEA as its launch partner for driverless long-haul trucking, aiming to begin commercial service before the end of 2025. The initial driverless runs will use the Houston‑to‑Frisco, Texas corridor that Kodiak has traveled daily with a safety driver for the past four years.
Kodiak reports it has logged close to 4 million miles of autonomous testing over more than seven years. To meet state requirements, Kodiak will integrate its trucks with PrePass’s weigh‑station bypass system, which will relay pre‑trip inspection data to enforcement officers as the vehicles approach inspection sites. Under the CVSA‑developed enhanced inspection standard for autonomous vehicles, each truck must undergo a near‑annual inspection every four days with zero defects permitted. The program will launch in Texas and Louisiana, with plans to expand along neighboring state freight corridors, and PrePass notes its bypass network has delivered over $12 billion in fleet savings over three‑plus decades.
“As we were thinking about who the right partners would be to launch that, IKEA was at the top of our list,” Daniel Goff, vice president of external affairs at Kodiak said.
“PrePass has previously attributed more than $12 billion in fleet savings over three-plus decades to its bypass network, primarily through fuel and time efficiencies,” Chas Wurster, chief technology officer at PrePass said.
Kodiak has been moving IKEA freight daily on the Houston‑to‑Frisco route with a safety driver for four years. Over more than seven years of testing, Kodiak has accumulated close to 4 million miles of autonomous operation.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/ikea-picks-kodiak-for-driverless-freight-rollout)

item.title: Owner-operators claim Red Line hid $1M+ in freight revenue
item.description:
On Sept. 17, a group of owner-operators filed a proposed class action lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, accusing Red Line Logistics and two executives of hiding freight revenue to pocket the difference. The lawsuit seeks more than $1 million in damages, alleging Red Line understated load values to keep the difference.
Under the lease agreements cited in the complaint, owner-operators were to receive 80% of the load value while Red Line kept 20%. The complaint says Red Line would bid $10,000 for a load but tell drivers the load was worth only $7,500, pocketing the $2,500 difference before calculating the driver’s share. To execute the scheme, Red Line allegedly entered actual load data into its Apex transportation management system, then instructed a dispatcher to reduce the value before entering it into the Sylectus system drivers used. The plaintiffs allege the false values were communicated through email, text and voice-over-internet-protocol messages, potentially numbering in the thousands over several years. The complaint also says the alleged conduct involved interstate and foreign commerce across the United States, Mexico and Canada, and that the plaintiffs have brought RICO claims accusing the defendants of wire fraud. As of the filing reviewed by FreightWaves, Red Line Logistics, Zaim Bajgoric and Anel Penava had not filed a response to the allegations in the publicly accessible docket.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/transportation-provider-accused-of-hiding-freight-revenue-from-owner-operators)

item.title: Alaska Air targets $750 million cargo revenue by 2030
item.description:
Alaska Airlines said it expects cargo revenue to reach $750 million by 2030, according to executives at an investor event on Wednesday. After merging with Hawaiian Airlines in September 2024, the carrier’s cargo revenue rose 57% to $549 million last year. In the first half of 2026, cargo revenue was $316 million, putting the airline on track for over $600 million for the full year.
The airline plans to lease four additional Boeing 737-800 converted freighters and will base two of them in Honolulu to run dedicated intra‑island service in Hawaii. Alaska Air also operates 11 Airbus A330-300 freighters for Amazon under a contract that was renegotiated earlier this year for more favorable terms. Internationally, the carrier serves five destinations today and will add Paris and Athens next year, aiming for 15 international ports by 2030 using Boeing 787-9s that carry cargo in the lower deck.
“Cargo allows us to fully monetize our assets across the network. As we grow internationally, optimize fleet deployment and leverage a combined Alaska and Hawaiian footprint, cargo becomes an increasingly meaningful contributor to both revenue growth and margin expansion,” Ian Morgan, vice president of cargo said.
“Cargo contributes as much as 20% of flight revenue on transpacific routes, creating meaningful revenue enhancement without additional aircraft. Collectively, these businesses produce margins that are twice the system average, making cargo an important contributor to our long term financial targets,” Ian Morgan, vice president of cargo said.
For years, cargo revenue was about a $130 million to $150 million annual business. After the merger with Hawaiian Airlines in September 2024, Alaska’s cargo revenue grew 57% to $549 million last year.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/alaska-air-eyes-50-share-of-intra-island-hawaii-cargo-market)

item.title: Maithili Shenoy urges retailers to cut supply chains as demand moves in days
item.description:
At the Sourcing Journal Fall Summit in New York City earlier this week, Maithili Shenoy warned that consumer demand now shifts in days. When production stayed near customers, lead times were short—usually 45 to 60 days. Shenoy said digital platforms can shift consumer demand in just days or weeks.
After global trade agreements expanded, brands moved production overseas to lower unit costs, which gradually lengthened supply chains. Longer lead times made forecasting harder, leading to excess inventory and frequent markdowns that eroded profit. Shenoy argued that judging health by margin percentages hides the real loss of dollar profit when lead times grow. She urged retailers to reset sourcing goals, measure profit in dollars, and shorten lead times to match the speed of demand. Retailers should align product development cycles with real‑time sales data to react faster to trends.
“Demand is largely moving in days, while the supply has gone in the opposite direction and moving in months,” Maithili Shenoy, founder and managing partner of the La Naia Group said.
“Percentages do not pay the bill, dollars do,” Maithili Shenoy, founder and managing partner of the La Naia Group said.
Before production moved overseas, apparel was made near consumers, giving short lead times and predictable seasonal demand. After trade agreements opened, brands shifted overseas to cut costs, which gradually lengthened supply chains and made forecasting harder.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/maithili-shenoy-sourcing-journal-fall-summit-adjusting-supply-chains-1239301232)

item.title: Kargo launches Karlo, an AI media‑buying platform for small businesses
item.description:
Kargo announced Thursday the general availability of Karlo, an AI media‑buying platform that drove a 21 percent lift in ad recall in an Ad Council pilot. The platform lets smaller teams plan, create and activate campaigns across the open web, CTV and social from a single system, with onboarding completed in just minutes.
Karlo is powered by Kargo’s Creative Science and Media Intelligence platforms, which combine premium audience data with contextual signals to inform bidding and targeting decisions. In real time, the tool scores and adjusts a business’s existing creative alongside bidding and targeting, treating creative as a performance lever rather than a static asset. By unifying CTV, social and open‑web buying in one flow, Karlo eliminates the need for separate buyers and lets campaigns be optimized while they are live.
“Creative usually sits outside that loop, untouched, even though it’s the biggest lever on performance,” Harry Kargman, founder and CEO of Kargo said.
“an innovative way to meaningfully engage an audience that can truly benefit from mental health messaging and resources,” DJ Perera, chief media officer at the Ad Council said.
Kargo has spent over two decades building AI‑powered advertising technology for large advertisers. Previously, smaller businesses lacked the budget and staff to access such tools, often needing separate buyers for CTV, social and the open web. Karlo makes the same capabilities available in a self‑serve format.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/kargo-launches-karlo-for-smbs-1239300495)

item.title: Rheom Materials launches Benree resin and Shorai Dura for footwear components
item.description:
On Oct. 1, Houston-based Rheom Materials announced it is introducing Benree resin for hard plastic shoe components and launching Shorai Dura, a footwear-grade leather alternative. Rheom said Benree passed SATRA testing for high-heel applications with Bared Footwear, showing performance comparable to ABS plastic. The company describes Benree as USDA Certified Biobased with 100 percent biobased content and says it biodegrades under home composting conditions.
Rheom reported Shorai Dura achieved up to 500,000 Bally Flex cycles and 70,000 Martindale abrasion revolutions in testing. A Los Angeles-based footwear manufacturer used Shorai Dura to create an athletic sneaker and a textured skater shoe, both prototypes. Benree is designed for injection molding applications, while Shorai Dura serves as a flexible material for parts traditionally made with leather or synthetic alternatives.
“A shoe is not one material; it is multiple parts working together as a system. Substituting a single material has never moved the needle,” Zimri T. Hinshaw, founder and CEO of Rheom Materials said.
“From samples and testing, Rheom has proven to be solving both of those problems for us,” Millie Richards, head of sustainability at Bared Footwear said.
Rheom Materials is moving deeper into footwear, targeting both the uppers shoppers see and the components beneath them. The expansion follows high-heel application testing with Australian brand Bared Footwear and the development of two prototype shoes featuring Shorai Dura uppers.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/rheom-materials-biobased-footwear-bared-shorai-benree-1239301219)

item.title: PwC reports 29% of shoppers will use AI for holiday gifts this year
item.description:
According to PwC’s 2026 Holiday Outlook, 29% of consumers plan to use AI throughout the holiday season for shopping, up from 20% last year. PwC projects overall holiday spending will rise 6-7% despite low consumer confidence, driven by Gen Z’s record store visits and a shift toward experiences and wellness.
Consumers are using AI for practical tasks such as research, product discovery, price checking, budget maintenance and understanding product features. Shoppers are spending more time crafting detailed prompts that outline recipients’ likes, dislikes, current possessions and lifestyle traits to generate hyper‑personalized gift lists. Gen Z shoppers aged 14‑29 are visiting physical stores in record numbers to interact with products and associates before completing purchases online. Spending is moving away from physical goods toward experiences and wellness, which PwC identifies as one of the fastest‑growing holiday gift categories.
“This year, our survey found that 29% of consumers plan to use AI throughout the holiday season for their shopping,” Kelly Pedersen, global retail leader at PwC U.S said.
“Despite what they indicate in sentiment surveys, we project consumers will actually spend 6-7% more this holiday season compared to last year,” Kelly Pedersen, global retail leader at PwC U.S said.
Last year’s PwC holiday survey found only 20% of shoppers planned to use AI, amid hype about automated purchasing that never materialized because major platforms held back on transaction mechanics. That unfulfilled hype has now normalized into a common tool for searching, comparing and shopping for holidays.
Source: Glossy (https://glossy.co/fashion/the-ai-powered-holiday-shopper-how-prompt-driven-curation-and-gen-alpha-algorithms-will-shape-consumer-behavior)

item.title: Skechers CFO John Vandemore joins Levi Strauss as CFO effective November 1
item.description:
John Vandemore, who spent nearly nine years as Skechers’ chief financial officer, will succeed Harmit Singh as Levi Strauss & Co.’s CFO starting November 1. The move comes as Levi’s aims to grow to $10 billion in annual revenue, a target also matched by Skechers’ recent sales figure.
Before joining Skechers, Vandemore held finance and operations leadership roles at Mattel, The Walt Disney Company, International Game Technology, and various consulting firms. Harmit Singh, who is retiring after many years at Levi’s, will remain as an adviser until November 30. Skechers’ revenue grew from $4 billion in 2017 to $10 billion in the most recent fiscal year, while Levi’s reported that direct‑to‑consumer sales accounted for just over half of its revenue in the latest quarter, rising 11% year‑over‑year.
“Mr. Vandemore previously served as the CFO of Skechers for 9 years, helping the company become one of the world’s largest footwear brands with over $9 billion in revenue,” Tom Nikic, Needham analyst said.
“John’s deep financial, operational and consumer experience, combined with his proven ability to help global brands scale and grow profitably, makes him the ideal partner to help us realize our ambition of becoming a $10 billion company,” Michelle Gass, Levi’s CEO said.
Harmit Singh announced his retirement as Levi Strauss & Co. CFO earlier this year and will stay on as an adviser until November 30. Under Vandemore’s tenure, Skechers’ revenue increased from $4 billion in 2017 to $10 billion in the most recent year, strengthening the shoe maker’s financial profile.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/skechers-cfo-jumps-levis/831872)

item.title: AI traffic to U.S. retail sites set to rise 130% this holiday season
item.description:
Adobe forecasts that AI-driven traffic to U.S. retail websites will increase 130% year over year during the upcoming holiday season Shoppers who use AI assistants generate 43% more revenue per visit than those who do not
More than three‑quarters of AI‑assisted shoppers say they feel more confident in their purchases. Over two‑thirds report they are less likely to return an item bought with an AI assistant’s help. AI‑referred visitors add items to their carts at a 32% higher rate than shoppers arriving through other channels.
“It also behaves as a discovery channel through AI search and a referral channel through the AI chatbots themselves,” Rebecca Wettemann said.
Eighteen months earlier Adobe’s research showed non‑AI traffic generated 128% more revenue per visit than AI‑referred visits. The projection comes from Adobe’s annual online shopping forecast, released Monday.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/consumer-ai-use-boon-holidays-ai-traffic-doubles/831790)

item.title: FreightWaves publishes October 2026 State of the Industry Report
item.description:
FreightWaves published its October 2026 State of the Industry Report, produced in affiliation with Ryder, offering an in-depth overview of the trucking, maritime and intermodal markets and outlook for the coming weeks. The report finds domestic intermodal volumes are nearly 9% above the prior year, attributing the gain to meaningful cost savings and network efficiencies.
Freight demand is described as steady overall, yet the market remains fragile with post‑Labor Day volatility showing how fast capacity and pricing can change. Import volumes stay strong, with major U.S. ports recording near‑record container activity as shippers continue to manage inventory levels carefully. Manufacturing continues to drive freight demand, as factory orders, industrial production and transportation equipment orders keep expanding despite moderating growth. Consumer spending has held up, but rising fuel costs and falling consumer sentiment could create headwinds for freight demand in the months ahead. Housing acts as a drag on freight markets, with declining home sales, reduced housing starts and weak builder sentiment weighing on construction‑related shipments. Transportation costs face upward pressure from fuel, as diesel prices hit record highs, lifting operating expenses and pushing freight rates higher across all modes. The report also notes that the data cover capacity, volumes and rates across trucking, maritime and intermodal segments, providing a breakdown for each. Accompanying the release, FreightWaves promoted its Brokerage Compliance Symposium, F3 Awards Dinner and the Future of Freight Festival, all set to take place in Chattanooga around the F3 event.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/white-paper-state-of-the-industry-october-2026)

item.title: Albertsons adds three directors and names interim CFO as board grows to 14
item.description:
Albertsons announced on Wednesday that it appointed three new directors and named Cody Perdue as interim CFO, expanding its board to 14 members. The new directors—Meg Ham, Bill Boltz and Chris Drumgoole—will start on Oct. 14, while Perdue succeeds Sharon McCollam, who remains an advisor until Feb. 27, 2027.
Before the additions, Albertsons’ board had 11 members, and after appointing Meg Whitman as executive chair last month it grew to 10, then to 14 with the three new directors. Ham retired in May 2025 after leading Food Lion for over a decade, Boltz oversees merchandising and omnichannel strategy for Lowe’s 1,700 U.S. stores, and Drumgoole manages operations and technology for Aligned Data Centers’ U.S. and Latin American facilities. Perdue joined Albertsons in 2023 and has been senior vice president of treasury, investor relations and risk management since 2025, a role he will keep while serving as interim CFO. Albertsons said it is still searching for a permanent CFO after McCollam’s planned retirement, which she announced in July.
“Albertsons is operating in an increasingly dynamic retail environment, and Bill, Chris and Meg bring expertise to our board that will help me and my team strengthen the business and serve customers,” Susan Morris, Albertsons’ CEO said.
“Cody has been my right hand and a trusted partner to the entire leadership team,” Sharon McCollam, former Albertsons president and CFO said.
Albertsons named Meg Whitman as executive chair last month. Albertsons pointed to weak sales growth and flat net sales in its most recent quarter amid a challenging environment for traditional grocers.
Source: Grocery Dive (https://grocerydive.com/news/albertsons-new-directors-interim-cfo-grocery/831877)

item.title: KnitWell Group names Angelica Munson chief digital and customer data officer
item.description:
KnitWell Group appointed Angelica Munson as its chief digital and customer data officer on September 22, according to a press release. In the newly created role, Munson will oversee customer data, insights, AI-assisted marketing tools, personalization and digital marketing for the company’s enterprise strategy.
Munson previously served as global chief digital officer at Shiseido Group, where she led the launch of the Beauty Tech Lab that offered AI-based skin diagnostics.
“Angelica is a highly respected digital and transformation leader whose experience sits at the intersection of customer insight, technology, marketing, and commerce,” Lizanne Kindler said.
KnitWell Group was created three years ago when Ann Taylor, Loft and Talbots were combined under a single holding company. Sycamore Partners acquired the Ascena brands Ann Taylor, Loft, Lane Bryant and Lou & Grey in the bankruptcy process and later purchased Chico’s FAS for $1 billion in 2024, adding White House Black Market and Soma to the group.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/knitwell-chief-digital-customer-data-officer-ann-taylor-chicos/831807)

item.title: Stripe to acquire embedded‑finance startup Parafin for $750 million
item.description:
Stripe announced it will acquire embedded‑finance startup Parafin, valued at $750 million, with the deal expected to close in the coming months. The purchase will let Stripe extend Parafin’s credit offerings to the more than 18,000 platforms that already use its payments network.
Parafin has extended roughly $3 billion in credit to about 60,000 U.S. and Canadian businesses since its first cash advance in 2021. The startup reported a $100 million annual revenue run rate as of December 2024 and had raised nearly $200 million in equity financing over its six‑year history. Stripe said the acquisition will strengthen its support for ambitious platforms while bringing more credit to the small businesses that drive economic growth.
“Platforms power millions of small businesses throughout the world and are central to Stripe’s mission,” Neetika Bansal, business lead at Stripe said.
“Offers, outstanding financing, and repayment terms are unaffected, and our combined scale and commitment will allow us to test more often, learn faster, and turn what works into better options for the platforms and businesses we serve,” Sahill Poddar and Vineet Goel, co‑founders of Parafin said.
Parafin was founded in 2020 on the premise that small and midsize businesses struggle to obtain loans because banks’ underwriting processes are designed for large enterprises, not because the businesses necessarily have poor credit. Since its launch, Parafin has raised nearly $200 million in equity financing, including a $100 million round in December 2024 that valued the company at $750 million.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/stripe-swallows-parafin/831903)

item.title: Fiserv launches stablecoin platform with North Dakota’s Roughrider Coin
item.description:
Fiserv went live this week with a stablecoin system that issues the Roughrider Coin, a digital asset backed by the Bank of North Dakota and designed for bank‑to‑bank transfers across the state’s interbank network. The platform will be accessible to roughly 90 financial institutions in North Dakota, letting them move funds using the digital currency while complying with state‑level regulatory expectations.
VersaBank issued the Roughrider coin, Fireblocks supplies the digital‑asset infrastructure and the Solana blockchain settles the transactions. Fiserv provides the issuance, reserve, custody and settlement layer for the stablecoin, handling the back‑end for participants. The system also supports payment cards linked to stablecoins, automated treasury workflows, tokenized deposits and currency‑exchange services for banks, corporations, online marketplaces and fintechs. Fiserv had previously disclosed plans to launch its own stablecoin, FIUSD, targeting its network of 10,000 financial institutions, six million merchant locations and roughly 90 billion annual transactions. The Roughrider coin, like other stablecoins, aims to reduce price volatility by being pegged to a stable asset such as the U.S. dollar.
“The launch of our digital asset platform is an important milestone for Fiserv and the financial institutions we serve,” Sunil Sachdev, Head of Embedded Finance and Digital Assets, Fiserv said.
“The new platform went live this week,” Fiserv spokesperson said.
North Dakota launched its own digital currency in October 2023, becoming the second U.S. state to do so after Wyoming’s Frontier Stable Token debuted in August 2023. Fiserv had previously announced plans to release its own stablecoin, FIUSD, by the end of 2023 to serve its network of 10,000 financial institutions, six million merchant locations and 90 billion annual transactions.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/fiserv-north-dakota-stablecoin-system-digital-asset/831901)

item.title: Consumer confidence drops to 12‑year low of 81.8 as inflation worries rise
item.description:
The Conference Board reported that the U.S. consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points this month to 81.8, marking a 12‑year low. Median inflation expectations for the next year rose 0.3 points to 5.1%, while the share of households expecting higher interest rates in the next 12 months jumped 5.2 points to 68.4%.
The drop reflects higher fuel prices, increased borrowing costs and employer hiring anxiety, according to the Conference Board. New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said there is no urgent need for another rate increase, projecting inflation to end 2026 at 3.5% and unemployment to ease from 4.1% to 4% over the coming year. Traders lowered the odds of a rate hike at the Oct. 28 Fed meeting to 47% from 71% on Monday, while a NABE survey showed 49% of economists view policy as too stimulative, up 38 points since February.
“Consumers are more disgruntled and squeezed in this economy than they felt during the 2020 pandemic,” Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union said.
The Conference Board noted that its survey aligned with the University of Michigan’s Friday release. Michigan’s survey showed consumer sentiment at a four‑month low and personal‑finance views down about 10%.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/consumer-confidence-sags-12-year-low-eroded-inflation-job-anxiety-fed-federal-reserve/831783)

item.title: PlusAI aims to close $800M Texas Ventures SPAC merger by year‑end
item.description:
PlusAI expects to finalize its merger with Texas Ventures Acquisition III Corp. before the close of the year, valuing the autonomous trucking developer at $800 million pre‑money. The deal could deliver as much as $300 million in cash to PlusAI, combining over $60 million of committed financing with a SPAC trust of roughly $236 million.
PlusAI’s HyperFoundry development platform generated $25 million in revenue this year and the company is targeting $40 million to $50 million in contracted revenue for 2026. The cash proceeds are expected to fund PlusAI’s operations through 2027, satisfying the deal’s minimum cash condition even if SPAC trust redemptions occur. Through a partnership with TRATON Group, PlusAI will integrate its Level 4 SuperDrive system into trucks sold under the International, Scania, MAN and Volkswagen Truck & Bus brands. Revenue from the SuperDrive system will be earned via a Driver‑as‑a‑Service model, leveraging TRATON’s existing manufacturing, sales and service networks. Liu said the company aims to launch driverless trucks commercially and begin scaling that effort in 2027, calling autonomous trucking the top priority despite the new platform.
“In terms of certainty of this transaction, it has very, very high certainty of closing in the coming months,” David Liu, co‑founder and CEO of PlusAI said.
“We are looking at launching driverless trucks commercially and starting to scale that in 2027,” David Liu, co‑founder and CEO of PlusAI said.
The merger follows PlusAI’s April termination of its deal with Churchill Capital Corp IX, which the company attributed to market conditions.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/plusai-texas-ventures-spac-close)

item.title: Walmart to open $300 million Ohio fulfillment center for oversized goods
item.description:
Walmart plans to build a $300 million fulfillment center in Turtlecreek Township, Ohio, according to a Sept. 28 press release from the Regional Economic Development Initiative Cincinnati. The facility will focus on televisions, furniture and other bulky items and is expected to generate more than 300 new jobs.
The facility will be built to handle bulky, non sortable merchandise such as televisions and furniture, allowing Walmart to keep such inventory closer to Midwest customers. It will sit on nearly 100 acres acquired in Warren County and is intended to work alongside the existing fulfillment center in Monroe, Ohio, which currently employs over 200 associates. The REDI Cincinnati announcement did not specify the building’s square footage or a construction timeline. This project fits into Walmart’s broader warehouse network revisions, which earlier this year included a proposal for a fulfillment warehouse of 1.5 million square feet in New York. Walmart also said it will spend more than $330 million to automate its Opelousas, Louisiana distribution center and will close fulfillment sites in Massachusetts and Illinois.
Earlier in 2026 Walmart sought to construct a fulfillment warehouse of 1.5 million square feet in New York and pledged over $330 million to upgrade its Opelousas, Louisiana distribution center with robotics. The retailer also announced plans to shut fulfillment centers in Massachusetts and Illinois, moves that come as Amazon and Costco expand their own big and bulky delivery offerings.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/walmart-to-build-ohio-fulfillment-center-for-oversized-goods/831792)

item.title: SH 130 toll road sees 130% truck traffic rise as fleets seek safer, faster route
item.description:
Heavy truck traffic on the southern 41‑mile stretch of SH 130 has risen nearly 130% since 2019, according to the road’s operator. Drivers on SH 130 are 80% less likely to experience a crash than those on I‑35, making it a safer alternative for fleets.
quotes
“The cost of time spent sitting in I-35 congestion — including increased fuel consumption, lost revenue and late fees for freight carriers — can be two to three times the cost of the SH 130 toll,” Ryan Sethness, Head of Freight Business Development, SH 130 Concession Company said.
context
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/sh-130-a-smarter-safer-route-through-central-texas)

item.title: Oxea chooses Uber Freight to run its global logistics network
item.description:
Oxea selected Uber Freight to manage its global logistics network, according to a Sept. 15 press release, while Uber Freight’s AI platform draws on data from more than 20 million delivered shipments. The logistics network spans the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and Europe, and Uber Freight will handle day-to-day transportation across truckload, rail, and ocean.
By anticipating disruptions earlier and coordinating regional and modal transportation, Uber Freight aims to improve on‑time performance and proactive communication for Oxea. Efficient routing from the integrated transportation management system can also help Oxea cut its carbon emissions. The TMS provides real‑time shipment visibility, access to Uber Freight’s public tracking portal and carrier performance dashboards. Uber Freight’s AI logistics platform supplies insight and data analysis from over 20 million shipments and answers industry‑specific questions in real time. Oxea’s Chief Supply Chain Officer Scott Farmer said the partnership lets the company stay focused on its core business while logistics expertise handles the network. The transportation management system can be integrated into Oxea’s enterprise resource planning system, enabling smooth data flow between logistics and core business processes.
“What matters is the impact: a clearer, earlier view of our global network, faster identification of potential disruptions, and more reliable, proactive information for customers,” Bret Bement, VP of supply chain management at Oxea said.
“We bring technology, data and logistics expertise together to run the operation, identify issues earlier and keep improving how the network performs,” D’Andrae Larry, Uber Freight Chief Commercial Officer said.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/chemical-manufacturer-selects-uber-freight-to-manage-global-logistics/831786)

item.title: H&M Kids launches Strawberry Thief childrenswear line with Morris & Co on 8 Oct
item.description:
H&M Kids has teamed up with Morris & Co to release a childrenswear collection featuring Strawberry Thief print, set to launch on 8 October in selected online markets. The line includes smocked dresses, matching sets and scalloped‑collar blouses in a palette of taupe, ivory, chestnut, dusky pink and deep teal, using brushed knit, corduroy and wool‑mix fabrics.
According to the brand, the collection captures the feeling of an English autumn, blending nostalgic heritage with modern wearability. Pieces are designed for everyday kidswear, aiming to feel rooted in craft but ready for real life.
“Our collaboration with Morris & Co. takes the storytelling of Strawberry Thief and brings it into everyday kidswear – pieces that feel rooted in craft but ready for real life. Together, we’ve created a collection that is about heritage made playful,” Sofia Löfstedt, head of kidswear design at H&M said.
“Strawberry Thief is all about celebrating the small, wild details in daily life, which felt like the perfect starting point for a children’s collection. The story of thrushes visiting the kitchen garden of Morris’ countryside home is an idyllic fairy tale in itself, and working with H&M brings these designs to a new generation, in pieces made to be worn, loved and lived in,” Jessica Clayworth, at Morris & Co said.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/hm-and-morris-co-collection)

item.title: Retailers pay 72p tax per £1 profit as sector’s tax bill hits £62bn
item.description:
Retailers and hospitality businesses paid 72p and 82p in tax for every £1 of pre‑tax profit respectively, with the two sectors together contributing £62bn in business taxes during 2025/26. Retail employment fell by 122,000 jobs and hospitality by 93,000 over the past two years.
The £62bn tax bill includes VAT, business rates, employer National Insurance contributions and other taxes. Retail and hospitality together account for almost a third of all revenue raised from the property tax, while one in seven high‑street properties nationwide is currently vacant. The BRC has warned that the rising tax burden is already causing job losses and shuttered shops, limiting the sector’s ability to invest and keep prices down. Ahead of the Budget, the BRC and UKHospitality are calling on Chancellor John Healey to ease the tax burden on high‑street firms, for example by taking retail and hospitality properties out of the government’s high‑value business rates multiplier.
“job losses,” Helen Dickinson, BRC chief executive said.
“more than 750,000 retail, hospitality and leisure properties already benefit from lower business rates multipliers,” Government spokesperson said.
The BRC previously said retail taxes have risen 20 percent over the past two years, leaving the sector paying £1.8bn more in business rates than it did two years ago. Ahead of the upcoming Budget, the BRC and UKHospitality are urging Chancellor John Healey to reduce the high‑street cost burden, including removing retail and hospitality properties from the government’s high‑value business rates multiplier.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/retailers-pay-72p-in-tax-for-every-1-of-profit)

item.title: H&M Group partners with Bleckmann to support UK expansion
item.description:
H&M Group has confirmed a new partnership with fashion logistics specialist Bleckmann to act as its third‑party logistics provider in the UK. The deal will see Bleckmann install an advanced AutoStore system at its Crick, Northamptonshire warehouse to boost flexibility, capacity and fulfilment efficiency.
The Crick site lies within Bleckmann’s Midlands ‘Golden Triangle’ network, where the logistics provider is making further investment to increase UK capacity. H&M will use the facility to manage logistics for a number of its brands, though the exact portfolio names were not disclosed. Bleckmann already handles logistics for fashion names such as Superdry, Gymshark and Blakely, and added sustainable footwear brand Nuoceans as a client in June. Earlier this year, dancewear brand Capezio also named Bleckmann its third‑party logistics provider for warehousing and distribution.
“essential to meeting the growing demand from existing and new clients,” Reinardt van Oel, chief operations officer for Belgium and the UK said.
“proud to now count H&M Group among our clients,” Reinardt van Oel, chief operations officer for Belgium and the UK said.
The site sits within Bleckmann’s Midlands ‘Golden Triangle’ network, with the group making further investment in its UK operations to boost capacity. Bleckmann already works with brands including Superdry, Gymshark and Blakely, while Belgian-British sustainable footwear brand Nuoceans appointed the business as its logistics partner in June.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/hm-group-taps-bleckmann-to-support-uk-expansion)

item.title: Kiehl’s opens 1,300‑sq‑ft experiential flagship on London’s Carnaby Street
item.description:
Kiehl’s has opened a 1,300‑sq‑ft experiential flagship on London’s Carnaby Street. The two‑storey unit marks Kiehl’s second standalone store in the West End and the first content studio the brand has launched in Europe.
The flagship features skin‑analysis technology, a photo booth and custom screen‑printing stations on the ground floor. An interactive Brew Bar matches skincare ingredients to customers’ moods and skin concerns, while Derma Readers provide personalised skin analysis. The entire upper floor is devoted to a content studio for creators, filming and community events, which Kiehl’s said is a first for the brand in Europe. Kiehl’s operates 18 boutiques across the UK, where Britain ranks among its three largest markets, and its Creamy Eye Treatment with Avocado is the UK’s best‑selling prestige eye cream according to L’Oréal.
“want to spend time in,” Niki Lo, UK general manager said.
“meaningful investment in the future of physical retail,” Melanie Vidal, global brand president said.
Kiehl’s is approaching its 175th anniversary and has been investing in standalone stores to boost customer acquisition, loyalty and brand engagement. It currently operates 18 boutiques in the UK, where Britain is one of the brand’s three largest markets.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/kiehls-opens-experiential-european-flagship-on-carnaby-street)

item.title: OpenAI’s ChatGPT ad measurement gaps keep marketer budgets at test level
item.description:
Seven months after OpenAI began selling ads in ChatGPT, marketers still struggle to measure campaign performance, leaving budgets at test levels. Agencies report that ChatGPT shows around 100 clicks while their own logs record only 20, and conversions appear 24 to 36 hours later than on Google.
Many advertisers have not enabled conversion tracking because signing OpenAI’s tracking terms raises legal concerns about liability and data use. OpenAI’s conversions API could improve attribution, but enterprise clients are slow to adopt it and smaller firms often lack the staff to set it up correctly. As a result, most campaigns are still optimized toward clicks or impressions rather than cost‑per‑acquisition or return on ad spend.
“The transition now that we are able to optimize to CPA, rather than focusing on CPC and leading metrics, has been pivotal,” Jellyfish’s Victor Batista, senior paid media director said.
“I think with time, as they gain confidence in their measurement suite, we will see further evolution, and platform confidence will improve as more data is analyzed across partners,” Jellyfish’s Victor Batista, senior paid media director said.
OpenAI introduced ads in ChatGPT seven months ago, but its measurement tools have remained basic, prompting marketer frustration.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/marketing/openais-measurement-gaps-are-keeping-chatgpt-ads-budgets-at-test-level)

item.title: Creators boost AI adoption to 87% as YouTube adds agentic tools
item.description:
Over the past year, 87% of creators have increased their use of AI in content creation, and 86% plan to raise it further in the next 12 months. This growth comes after an early‑year rejection of AI‑generated content and coincides with YouTube’s addition of agentic features such as video A/B testing and conversational editing.
YouTube’s new Ask Studio tool, powered by Gemini, lets creators upload multiple video versions and predicts which version will keep viewers watching the longest. CapCut and Adobe Firefly provide AI‑driven editing suites that creators use for tasks ranging from brainstorming to file organization, while brands worry that AI‑flagged posts could trigger platform penalties dubbed “AI jail”. Creators such as Gigi Robinson employ AI for analytics and task management, yet concerns persist that heavy reliance on generative AI could erode authenticity and lead to homogeneous content.
“I think it’s a lot harder to be super binary because it’s just crept into our everyday so much,” Lucy Kruszynski said.
“I don’t think brands care outside of like, ‘is this content going to be flagged as AI? And if it is, will I get into AI jail or algorithm jail?’ That’s the tricky part,” Keith Bendes said.
Earlier in the year, after the release of OpenAI’s Sora 2, the creator economy loudly denounced generative AI content in favor of authenticity. YouTube removed AI slop accounts, Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri issued a memo urging higher ranking for originality, and brands sought the messiness and creativity of real creators.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/media/the-creator-economys-stance-on-ai-is-shifting-again)

item.title: Amazon says 20% of brand value appears after ad attribution window closes.
item.description:
Amazon says about 20% of a brand’s sales value appears after the standard 7‑ to 30‑day ad attribution window ends, based on a study of over two million June campaigns. The finding underpins Amazon’s push to count ad impact over a full year, using a long‑term sales metric first tested in a closed beta since October 2024.
The metric tracks new‑to‑brand shoppers, notes their first ad‑driven actions like a brand search or cart add, and applies the brand’s past 12‑month return from similar shoppers to forecast annual sales. Amazon has also rolled out full‑funnel campaigns, announced last November, that shift budgets across Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, display and streaming to encourage longer‑term purchases. Soon marketers will be able to compare projected long‑term sales with actual results in Amazon’s clean room, while the platform now provides agencies with 90 days of historical sales data—short of the roughly 18 months many models require.
“What we actually find is that roughly 20% of the sales value for a brand shows up over time and isn’t captured in that immediate attribution window because that’s just a cutoff date for measurement,” Lily Tong, a director of measurement at Amazon Ads said.
Amazon believes its advertising drives more sales than the short attribution windows currently show. Demonstrating that longer‑term impact is becoming a basic requirement, and Amazon faces the same pressure as Google to prove it. While improved upper‑funnel tools and AI shopping shift spend away from search, platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and creators often claim credit for purchases that ultimately occur on Amazon.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/media-buying/amazon-wants-to-own-the-long-game-in-ad-measurement)

item.title: AI agents show 177 toy brands but nearly all picks come from Amazon’s own store
item.description:
Jellyfish’s Share of Model tool found that Alexa for Shopping recommended toys from 177 brands, with nearly all selections coming from Amazon’s own store. By contrast, ChatGPT suggested 24 retailers and Google’s AI Mode suggested 37 for the same toy request.
The Share of Model tool tracked recommendations from Alexa, ChatGPT and Google’s AI Mode across eight categories in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia and Singapore. In July, Copilot’s top 100 e-commerce sites accounted for 34% of its citations, a share more than triple Google’s AI Mode and eight times ChatGPT’s. A Dentsu Creative survey of 1,950 senior marketers in 14 markets found 59% are optimizing content for AI-enabled search while half are investing in agentic commerce. Adobe’s analysis of more than one trillion U.S. retail site visits showed AI-referred shoppers generated 53% higher revenue per visit than other traffic in July.
The article describes AI agents as emerging gatekeepers that choose products for shoppers using algorithms marketers do not fully understand. It notes that marketers have begun tailoring content and investing in agentic commerce to improve visibility in those AI-driven recommendations.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/marketing/in-graphic-detail-where-brands-stand-when-ai-agents-do-the-shopping)

item.title: Favorite Daughter uses creator content to boost growth since 2020 launch
item.description:
Favorite Daughter, a women’s clothing brand launched in 2020 by sisters Erin and Sara Foster, says creator-led content is driving its growth. In one Instagram post, Galvan showcases five work shirts she calls 1,000,000% worth the money. The brand began working with creators ahead of its National Daughters Day campaign on September 25.
Favorite Daughter appointed Laura Galvan as its dedicated social-media head, and she appears in multiple videos each week.
“The intent really wasn’t for [Galvan] to be public-facing,” Jennifer Stender Hawkins, EVP of Favorite Daughter and Centric Brands said.
“I think there’s not much [that’s] more important than having a creator on staff,” Jennifer Stender Hawkins, EVP of Favorite Daughter and Centric Brands said.
Creator partnerships have been used by retailers for years, but recent months have seen a surge in formal programs.
Source: Modern Retail (https://modernretail.co/marketing/it-scared-the-hell-out-of-me-to-hand-over-the-keys-what-brands-have-learned-from-creator-partnerships)

item.title: Seeteria AI uses existing warehouse cameras to cut idle dock time
item.description:
Seeteria’s AI platform flags idle dock doors that sit for as long as 7 minutes, helping warehouses recover lost capacity without new hardware. Small disruptions of 7 to 15 minutes each can compound into hours of missed capacity per shift, according to the founder.
The platform connects to a facility’s existing camera network over Wi‑Fi, analyzes activity in real time, and sends color‑coded alerts — green, yellow, red — to supervisors’ mobile or tablet apps showing the status of each dock door and zone. Floor supervisors receive live push alerts, warehouse managers get a post‑shift summary of bottlenecks, and executives view a financial‑impact report tied to detention fees and missed throughput targets. The system deliberately avoids identifying people, detecting only objects such as forklifts, pallets, dock doors and congestion patterns to protect worker privacy and reduce surveillance anxiety.
“Our goal all the time is to get the warehouse more capacity from the resources that they are already paying for,” Sarit Tamir, founder and CEO of Seeteria said.
“The system is completely blind to people,” Sarit Tamir, founder and CEO of Seeteria said.
Seeteria recently completed a stint at the CoLab accelerator in Chattanooga, Tennessee, after a connection made at the Home Delivery World conference in Nashville. The company announced that a new pilot launch in Chattanooga is imminent. Its name derives from the Greek goddess Soteria, but the spelling was changed from “SO” to “SEE” to reflect its computer vision focus.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/warehouse-ai-using-existing-cameras-to-cut-idle-dock-time)

item.title: DoorDash shows off under‑55‑pound delivery drone for Northern California launch
item.description:
DoorDash showed off its in‑house delivery drone on Tuesday, a six‑rotor craft weighing under 55 pounds. The drone is slated to begin deliveries in Northern California within months, carrying light orders three to five miles.
It weighs less than Amazon’s Prime Air drone, which the company lists at roughly 78 pounds. Its slow‑spinning propellers were shaped to produce a sound comparable to a passing car, aiming to reduce noise complaints. DoorDash said the first restaurant partners will be Chipotle and Popeyes. The three‑to‑five‑mile range is expected to cover about 80 % of typical DoorDash orders.
“The six-rotor drone comes in under 55 pounds, compared with the roughly 78 pounds Amazon lists for its Prime Air drone, and its slow-spinning propellers were designed so it sounds about like a passing car,” Stanley Tang, co‑founder and chief product officer said.
“The design was built around noise from the start, as Amazon’s drones face complaints from residents about their buzzing,” Harrison Shih, DoorDash Air head said.
DoorDash designed the drone in-house for its DoorDash Air service. Amazon’s Prime Air drone has drawn complaints from residents about its buzzing noise.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/doordash-unveils-its-own-delivery-drone-which-it-says-is-lighter-and-quieter-than-amazons-ahead-of-a-northern-california-launch)

item.title: Meta launches Muse for Small Business
item.description:
Meta launched Muse for Small Business, extending its Muse personal AI agent—released in the United States and Canada earlier this month—to help owners run their businesses. Owners can link Shopify, Stripe, Intuit QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Canva, Slack, and other tools, along with Facebook Pages, Instagram professional analytics, and Meta ad accounts. From there, they can assign goals such as building a growth plan from a year of sales and campaigns, drafting next week’s ads, or flagging expenses that look wrong, with all actions pending owner approval.
Muse itself is free to use, though paid subscription plans are available for owners who need additional features. The system does not publish, send, or process payments until the owner explicitly approves each output.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/meta-launches-muse-for-small-business-connecting-its-ai-agent-to-shopify-stripe-quickbooks-klaviyo-and-meta-ad-accounts)
